output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Thank you for keeping my bag safe and for calling the number on my lab manual to reach me. I genuinely appreciate that you made the effort to contact me instead of leaving the bag behind or throwing it away.

I am writing about the black Jansport bag I forgot in the Oshodi–Igando danfo on Friday evening, 6 November, when I got down at Ikotun. It contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, I am a first-year Biology student, and I urgently need these items for my BIO 101 practical on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m. We are not allowed into the practical without our dissecting kits, and the lab attendant is very strict about this. My ID card and glasses are also important for my classes.

I can offer ₦10,000 towards your transport and as a sincere thank-you for keeping the bag safe. That is all I can manage from my allowance. I do not have ₦40,000, and I cannot promise to send money that I do not have.

You were kind and reassuring during our first call, so I was worried when you later said I should pay ₦40,000 or forget the bag. I respectfully ask you to reconsider. I appreciate your help, but ₦40,000 is not an amount I can afford, and I do not believe payment of that amount should be a condition for returning my belongings.

Please choose a convenient day and time before Wednesday for us to meet in daylight at Ikotun roundabout or, if you prefer, by the gate of Ikotun Police Division—simply as a public, easy-to-find meeting point. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me, and I can give you the ₦10,000 when you hand over the bag.

Please reply to confirm which location and time would suit you. Thank you again for keeping my belongings safe. I hope we can resolve this respectfully.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your name]
